label: FICTIONAL and SYNTHETIC: Kestrel example, not real data

types.name: Password reset
types.risk_example: Low: customer stays locked out a little longer
types.reason: 99.8% accurate and a wrong call costs little

examples.message: I've forgotten my password and the reset email isn't arriving.
examples.proposed: I've sent a new reset link to the email you log in with. If it isn't in your inbox in a few minutes, check your spam folder for an email from Gusta. The link works for 30 minutes.
examples.rule: Forgotten password: send one reset link. If it hasn't arrived, ask the customer to check spam for an email from Gusta.
examples.verdict_reason: Sent one new link and pointed to the spam folder.

examples.message: Can you reset my password? I've lost access to my old work email.
examples.proposed: I can't change the email you log in with, but your account owner can, under Settings > Users. Once they've updated it, I'll send a reset link to the new address.
examples.rule: Never change the email someone logs in with. Only the account owner can, under Settings > Users.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't change the login email; pointed to the account owner.

examples.message: Reset link says expired.
examples.proposed: Sorry about that. I've sent you a fresh reset link.
examples.rule: Reset links expire after 30 minutes. Say so every time you send one.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't mention the 30-minute limit; the customer opened the link an hour later and it had expired again.

types.name: Can't log in
types.risk_example: Low: customer tries again or asks for a person
types.reason: 98.1% accurate and a wrong call costs little

examples.message: My 2-step code isn't arriving by text.
examples.proposed: I've sent your code by email instead. So texts work next time, check your phone number under Profile > Security.
examples.rule: 2-step code not arriving by text: send it by email instead, and show where to update the phone number (Profile > Security).
examples.verdict_reason: Sent the code by email and showed where to fix the phone number.

examples.message: It says my account is locked.
examples.proposed: Your account locked after 5 failed attempts. It unlocks by itself in 15 minutes; I've sent a reset link so you can choose a new password then.
examples.rule: Accounts lock for 15 minutes after 5 failed attempts. Explain the wait and send a reset link.
examples.verdict_reason: Explained the 15-minute wait and sent a reset link.

examples.message: I can't log in on my phone but it works on my laptop.
examples.proposed: Try clearing the app's cache: open your phone's settings, find Gusta and tap Clear cache.
examples.rule: Can't log in on the mobile app only: check the app version first. If it's out of date, ask them to update before anything else.
examples.verdict_reason: Skipped the version check; the app was 3 versions out of date and needed an update.

types.name: Missing payslip
types.risk_example: Low: wrong month resent, employee asks again
types.reason: 99.4% accurate and a wrong call costs little

examples.message: One of my staff can't find her March payslip.
examples.proposed: Open her profile under Employees, then Documents. Her March payslip is there, and you can resend it to her from the same page.
examples.rule: Payslips are on each employee's profile under Documents. Admins can resend them from there.
examples.verdict_reason: Pointed to the right page and offered the resend.

examples.message: Where do employees download payslips?
examples.proposed: Employees download their payslips in the Gusta employee app, under Payslips. Here's a guide you can share with your staff: Getting started with the employee app.
examples.rule: Employees download their own payslips in the Gusta employee app. Share the employee app guide.
examples.verdict_reason: Pointed to the employee app and shared the guide.

examples.message: Payslips for last Friday aren't showing.
examples.proposed: I've resent last Friday's payslips to all your employees.
examples.rule: Payslips missing for a recent run: check the run status first. Payslips only exist once a run is approved.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't check the run: it was still a draft, so there were no payslips to send.

types.name: Update company address
types.risk_example: Medium: tax letters go to the old address
types.reason: 99.0% accurate and a wrong call is easy to fix

examples.message: We've moved office, how do I change our address?
examples.proposed: As the account owner, you can change it under Settings > Company > Addresses. If both have moved, update the registered address (where tax letters go) and the trading address (shown on payslips).
examples.rule: Only the account owner can change the registered address, which tax letters go to. Admins can change the trading address.
examples.verdict_reason: Checked the person is the account owner before giving the steps.

examples.message: Change our trading address to 14 Mill Lane.
examples.proposed: You can update it under Settings > Company > Addresses > Trading address. Your registered address, where tax letters go, stays as it is.
examples.rule: The registered and trading addresses are separate. Change or explain only the one the customer asked about.
examples.verdict_reason: Dealt only with the trading address, as asked.

examples.message: Our address on payslips is wrong.
examples.proposed: You can correct it under Settings > Company > Addresses > Registered address.
examples.rule: Payslips show the trading address, not the registered address.
examples.verdict_reason: Pointed to the registered address; payslips show the trading address.

types.name: Add a new employee
types.risk_example: Medium: employee set up on the wrong pay schedule
types.reason: 96.4% accurate: good, but not enough to send unchecked

examples.message: How do I add someone starting Monday?
examples.proposed: Go to Employees > Add employee. Before their first payroll run, you'll need their tax code, ID number, start date and bank details.
examples.rule: Before a new employee's first payroll run, Gusta needs their tax code, ID number, start date and bank details.
examples.verdict_reason: Listed all four details needed before the first run.

examples.message: New starter is part time, 3 days a week.
examples.proposed: When you add them, set their contracted days to 3. Gusta then pays 3/5 of the full-time salary.
examples.rule: Part-time staff: set their contracted days. Salary is pro-rata to a 5-day week.
examples.verdict_reason: Set contracted days so the salary is pro-rata.

examples.message: Adding a weekly-paid worker to our monthly payroll.
examples.proposed: Add them under Employees > Add employee and choose your monthly pay schedule.
examples.rule: Each employee is on one pay schedule. Weekly-paid staff need a weekly schedule; if the account has none, create it first under Settings > Pay schedules.
examples.verdict_reason: Put a weekly-paid worker on the monthly schedule; the account had no weekly schedule, so one was needed first.

types.name: Change bank details
types.risk_example: High: payroll paid from or to the wrong account
types.reason: 98.7% accurate, but a wrong call is costly, so a support agent checks

examples.message: We've switched banks, need to update the account payroll is paid from.
examples.proposed: I've started the change under Settings > Bank account. It takes effect once your account owner approves it and our team confirms it on a short verification call.
examples.rule: Changing the company bank account needs the account owner's approval and a verification call from Gusta before it takes effect.
examples.verdict_reason: Asked for the owner's approval and the verification call.

examples.message: An employee gave me new bank details.
examples.proposed: You can update them on the employee's profile under Bank details. Please check the new details against the bank form they signed before saving.
examples.rule: Admins change an employee's bank details on their profile. The new details must match the bank form the employee signed.
examples.verdict_reason: Asked for the check against the signed form.

examples.message: Change our company account number, urgent, payroll is tomorrow.
examples.proposed: I've started the change so it's ready for tomorrow's run. Your account owner needs to approve it first.
examples.rule: No bank changes within 3 working days of a payroll run. Hand over to a support agent for a manual check.
examples.verdict_reason: Payroll was 1 working day away; inside 3 days it should have gone to a support agent for a manual check.

examples.message: You charged us twice this month.
examples.proposed: I can see two identical charges on your November invoice. I've refunded the second one in full.
examples.rule: Duplicate charge: confirm it on the invoice, then refund the duplicate in full.
examples.verdict_reason: Confirmed the duplicate on the invoice, then refunded it in full.

examples.message: We cancelled on 20 February but were still billed for February.
examples.proposed: Sorry about that. I've refunded February's charge in full.
examples.rule: Cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing month. That month is still charged.
examples.verdict_reason: February was still due: the cancellation only took effect at the end of February.

examples.message: Can I get a refund for the unused months on our annual plan?
examples.proposed: Annual plans can get a pro-rata refund for unused months. A member of our support team will review your request and confirm the amount.
examples.rule: Annual plans: refunds for unused months are pro-rata and reviewed by a support agent before they're paid.
examples.verdict_reason: Sent the pro-rata refund for a support agent to review.

examples.message: Payroll failed with a bank error.
examples.proposed: Your bank authorisation expired on 1 November. Renew it under Settings > Bank account > Authorisation, then rerun payroll from Payroll > Runs.
examples.rule: Bank error on a run: check the bank authorisation first. If it has expired, show how to renew it, then rerun.
examples.verdict_reason: Found the expired authorisation before suggesting a rerun.

examples.message: Run failed, says tax code missing for 2 employees.
examples.proposed: Priya Shah and Tom Ellis have no tax code. Add them on each profile under Tax, then rerun payroll.
examples.rule: Missing tax codes: name the employees and where to add the codes, then rerun.
examples.verdict_reason: Named both employees and where to add the codes.

examples.message: Payroll didn't go through and staff are asking where their pay is.
examples.proposed: Sorry about that. Rerun payroll from Payroll > Runs and your staff will be paid.
examples.rule: Before suggesting any rerun, check whether the payment was already sent. If it was, never rerun; hand over to a support agent.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't check the payment: it had already been sent, so a rerun would pay staff twice.

types.name: Tax form question
types.risk_example: High: customer files a wrong figure and gets a penalty
types.reason: Costly if wrong and only 94% accurate

examples.message: Where do I find the year-end tax forms for my staff?
examples.proposed: They're under Reports > Year end. From there you can download them or send each employee their form.
examples.rule: Year-end forms are under Reports > Year end. Admins send them to employees from there.
examples.verdict_reason: Gave the right place and how to send the forms.

examples.message: Why is the tax on this form different from the payslips?
examples.proposed: The form includes a correction made in November, after this employee's tax code changed. Payslips before November show the old figures.
examples.rule: A form differs from the payslips: check for corrections in that tax year before answering.
examples.verdict_reason: Found the November correction before answering.

examples.message: Do I need to file anything for a contractor?
examples.proposed: Yes: add them under Employees and they'll be included in your year-end filing.
examples.rule: Contractors are not employees: they aren't paid through payroll and use a separate contractor form. Never give the employee process for a contractor.
examples.verdict_reason: Gave the employee process for a contractor.

types.name: Cancel subscription
types.risk_example: High: account and payroll history closed by mistake
types.reason: 98.9% accurate, but a wrong call is costly, so a support agent checks

examples.message: We're closing the business, how do I cancel?
examples.proposed: Sorry to see you go. First run your final payroll, then export your records under Reports > Export all. Once your account owner confirms, I'll set up the cancellation.
examples.rule: Before cancelling: run the final payroll, export the records (Reports > Export all), and the account owner confirms.
examples.verdict_reason: Covered final payroll, export and the owner's confirmation.

examples.message: Cancel at the end of this month please.
examples.proposed: I've set your cancellation for the end of this billing month; this month is still charged. Before then, export your records under Reports > Export all.
examples.rule: Cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing month. That month is still charged.
examples.verdict_reason: Cancelled for the end of the billing month and said it's still charged.

examples.message: Thinking of cancelling, what happens to our data?
examples.proposed: Your records are deleted when your account closes, so export anything you need first.
examples.rule: Records are kept, read-only, for 6 years after cancelling, then deleted.
examples.verdict_reason: Records are kept read-only for 6 years, not deleted at closing.

types.name: Change pay date
types.risk_example: High: staff paid on the wrong day

examples.message: Can we pay staff on the 25th instead of the last day?
examples.proposed: Yes. Change it under Settings > Pay schedules; it applies from your next run. Approve each run at least 2 working days before the 25th so the bank pays on time.
examples.rule: A new pay date applies from the next run. Runs must be approved 2 working days before the pay date (the bank cut-off).
examples.verdict_reason: Applied it from the next run and gave the bank cut-off.

examples.message: Bank holiday on payday, can we pay a day early?
examples.proposed: Yes. I've moved this month's pay date to the working day before the bank holiday.
examples.rule: Payday on a bank holiday: pay on the working day before.
examples.verdict_reason: Moved pay to the working day before.

examples.message: Move this month's pay date to tomorrow.
examples.proposed: Done: this month's pay date is now tomorrow.
examples.rule: A pay date can't move inside the 2-working-day bank cut-off.
examples.verdict_reason: Tomorrow was inside the 2-working-day bank cut-off; staff would have been paid late.

types.name: Invoice question
types.risk_example: Low: customer is confused about a charge
types.reason: 98.3% accurate and a wrong call costs little

examples.message: What is this extra charge on our invoice?
examples.proposed: That line is for 2 employees added on 12 November, charged pro-rata for the rest of the month.
examples.rule: Explain invoice charges line by line, using the invoice breakdown.
examples.verdict_reason: Explained the line from the invoice breakdown.

examples.message: Can I get a copy of last month's invoice?
examples.proposed: Here's your October invoice. You'll always find invoices under Settings > Billing > Invoices.
examples.rule: Invoices are under Settings > Billing > Invoices.
examples.verdict_reason: Sent the invoice and showed where invoices are kept.

examples.message: Why did our price go up?
examples.proposed: Gusta raised prices for all customers this year.
examples.rule: Before explaining a price change, check the account's plan history.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't check the plan history: they had moved to a bigger plan in September.

examples.message: How is holiday pay worked out for part-time staff?
examples.proposed: It's pro-rata to their contracted days: someone on 3 days a week gets 3/5 of the full-time holiday.
examples.rule: Part-time holiday is pro-rata to contracted days.
examples.verdict_reason: Explained the pro-rata rule with an example.

examples.message: An employee says her holiday pay is too low.
examples.proposed: I've checked: her holiday pay matches her basic pay for those days, so it's correct.
examples.rule: Holiday pay includes regular overtime and regular commission, not just basic pay.
examples.verdict_reason: Left out the regular overtime she works every month, so she was underpaid.

examples.message: How do I record 2 days of leave?
examples.proposed: Open the employee's profile, go to Leave and add the 2 days on their calendar.
examples.rule: Leave is recorded on the employee's profile under Leave.
examples.verdict_reason: Pointed to the Leave page.

types.name: Export payroll report
types.reason: 98.5% accurate and a wrong call costs little

examples.message: Need a payroll summary for our accountant.
examples.proposed: Here's your payroll summary for the last full tax year, as a spreadsheet. Tell me if your accountant needs different dates.
examples.rule: Payroll summary: default to the last full tax year unless the customer gives dates.
examples.verdict_reason: Defaulted to the last full tax year.

examples.message: How do I export last quarter?
examples.proposed: Go to Reports > Payroll summary, set the dates to April to June, and click Export.
examples.rule: "Last quarter" means the most recent full calendar quarter.
examples.verdict_reason: The ticket came in October; the most recent full quarter was July to September.

examples.message: Can I get a list of all employees with salaries?
examples.proposed: Here's the list of your 24 employees with their salaries.
examples.rule: Only the account owner and admins can export salaries.
examples.verdict_reason: Checked the person is an admin before exporting salaries.

types.name: Pension deduction question
types.risk_example: Medium: wrong deduction explained to staff

examples.message: Why has pension been taken from a new starter?
examples.proposed: New starters join your workplace pension automatically after a 3-month waiting period. Sam's ended in October, so deductions started this month.
examples.rule: New starters are enrolled in the workplace pension automatically after a 3-month waiting period.
examples.verdict_reason: Explained the waiting period using Sam's dates.

examples.message: An employee wants to opt out of the pension.
examples.proposed: Record the opt-out on their profile under Pension. As they're within a month of enrolment, their deductions will be refunded in the next run.
examples.rule: Opt-outs within a month of enrolment get their deductions refunded in the next run.
examples.verdict_reason: Recorded the opt-out and the refund.

examples.message: Pension amount looks wrong this month.
examples.proposed: This month's pension deduction is the same as last month's, so it looks right.
examples.rule: Before confirming a pension deduction is right, check for salary changes that month.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't check for salary changes: a pay rise this month hadn't reached the pension, so the deduction was too low.
